title: Downtown community planning permit by-law approved
subtitle: Also: College Avenue East student housing, 81 College Avenue West rezoning, site plan by-law, heritage notice.
overview: Council approved a new community planning permit system for downtown Guelph {{vote:m19}}. It replaces the zoning by-law in the downtown area and combines zoning, minor variance and site plan approvals into one process. Staff say this will speed up decisions. It also includes an official plan amendment and updated planning fees.

The most contested issue was affordable housing tied to extra building height. Council defeated a proposal to restore a stronger sliding-scale requirement {{vote:m12}}. It also defeated a proposal to apply the requirement only above the heights already approved in the downtown height study {{vote:m16}}, and one to extend the transition period to three years {{vote:m15}}. Staff's recommended approach stayed in place.

Council approved the rezoning for a place of worship with a daycare and residence at 81 College Avenue West {{vote:m8}}. It received a first application for a 10-storey student apartment building at 210, 214 and 222 College Avenue East {{vote:m7}}, with no decision yet. Council also deferred the 115 Watson Parkway North decision to May 12 at the applicant's request {{vote:m2}}. A closed session on land use planning matters ended with council receiving information.

decisions.detail: Council approved the city-initiated downtown community planning permit by-law, repealed the existing zoning for the downtown area, approved the related official plan amendment and planning fee changes, and decided no further public notice was needed {{vote:m19}}.
Council defeated an amendment that would have set affordable housing requirements of 5%, 10% and 33% depending on additional storeys, with a cash-in-lieu option {{vote:m12}}.

decisions.item: Affordable housing only above approved heights
decisions.detail: Council defeated an amendment to apply a 5% requirement only to bonus height above the heights approved in OPA 106, up to 20% more {{vote:m16}}.
Council defeated an amendment to lengthen the by-law's transition period to three years {{vote:m15}}.

Council approved rezoning to a Neighbourhood Institutional zone with site-specific provisions for a three-storey place of worship with a daycare and an attached residence with an additional dwelling unit {{vote:m8}}.
Council received the statutory public meeting report on proposed official plan and zoning amendments for a 10-storey student rental building; no decision was made {{vote:m7}}.
Council approved a new site plan control by-law with delegated approval authority, repealing the 1986 site plan by-law, and amended the delegation of authority by-law.
Council deferred the decision on the zoning amendment and draft plan of subdivision to the May 12, 2026 planning meeting at the applicant's request {{vote:m2}}.

debate: Supporters of stronger affordable housing requirements said the city's housing affordability strategy had unanimous support and that a 5% requirement would yield very few units in a large building. They also noted the city's significant downtown infrastructure spending.

Development-industry delegates said mandatory affordable housing requirements on already-approved heights could stall projects, questioned the legal authority for them, and argued the economic analysis did not reflect site conditions such as brownfield clean-up. One delegate suggested bonusing only above approved heights.

Staff said they had already reduced the requirement significantly after feedback, that a related project in another planning permit area was proceeding with a higher requirement, and that results would be reported annually. They said they were open to further talks on variations and site-specific items.

Neighbours of 81 College Avenue West raised concerns about tree protection, parking, drainage and consultation. The applicant committed to meeting them and to no road salt in the parking area, and staff said tree issues would be addressed at site plan.

On the College Avenue East student housing, a neighbouring golf club raised concerns about shadows, wind, parking spillover and stray golf balls. Councillors asked staff to look at density, stormwater, a crosswalk, bus stops and drive aisle widths.
